c.tagline: Swedish-speaking island capital of Åland, all sailing ships, cycling, and Baltic archipelago calm.

taxi.fareNote: Uber has no meaningful presence; metered taxis are booked by phone (Taxi Åland) or picked up at ranks near the harbours and centre.

emergency.note: 112 is the single EU emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_desc: The walkable heart of town around the Torggatan and Nygatan shopping streets and the linden-lined Esplanade, with shops, cafes, and the town hall; the natural base for first-timers.
The Western Harbour, Mariehamn's international ferry port and maritime showpiece, home to the four-masted barque Pommern and the Åland Maritime Museum; best for sights and sea history.
The Eastern Harbour, home to Sjökvarteret — a working boatbuilding quarter — one of Scandinavia's largest marinas, and a quieter waterside feel; good for a calmer, nautical stay.
A leafy residential peninsula south of the centre with quiet lanes, shoreline paths, and easy cycling; suits families and travelers wanting a relaxed local base.

water.note: Tap water is excellent and safe to drink.

transit.hours: Ålandstrafiken regional buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM on weekdays, with reduced weekend service, radiating from central stops on Torggatan.
transit.note: Mariehamn is flat and famously bike-friendly — most people cycle. Green Ålandstrafiken buses (lines 1-5) connect the town to the rest of the main island, and taxis fill late-night gaps.
transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash to the driver or with a rechargeable travel card; single tickets start around €3.

transit.m: Taxi to the city centre (~5 min)
Several downtown hotels offer free airport pickup on request

tip.r: Service is included in prices; rounding up or leaving ~5-10% for good service is appreciated but not expected.

landmarks: Museum Ship Pommern
A perfectly preserved 1903 four-masted grain windjammer moored in the western harbor, the world's only such ship kept in original condition.
Åland Maritime Museum
One of the world's finest small maritime museums celebrates the age of sail with figureheads, ship models and tales of Cape Horn voyages.
Sjökvarteret (Maritime Quarter)
A living harbor quarter of boatbuilders' sheds, smithies and traditional wooden ships where Åland's archipelago craft traditions continue daily.
St. Göran's Church
Mariehamn's 1927 red-granite church, designed by Lars Sonck, displays luminous frescoes and Nordic Art Nouveau restraint amid linden-lined streets.
Åland Cultural History and Art Museum
The islands' flagship museum pairs 7,000 years of archipelago history with Åland art, explaining the autonomy that makes this Finnish province unique.
Lilla Holmen
A beloved bathing islet reached by footbridge from the eastern harbor, complete with sandy beach, strutting peacocks and picnic lawns.
The Esplanade (Storagatan)
A stately linden avenue linking the town's two harbors, flanked by carved wooden villas from Mariehamn's Russian spa-town era.
Badhusparken and Badhusberget
The leafy western-harbor park where 19th-century spa guests once promenaded, now offering sunset views over Pommern and the sailing harbor.
Ramsholmen Nature Reserve
A small forested islet a few kilometers from town, laced with a coastal walking path and known for wild garlic and abundant birdlife.
Mariehamn Town Hall (Stadshuset)
A 1939 building designed by architect Lars Sonck overlooking Stadshusbacken park, long the seat of Mariehamn's municipal government.

train.note: There is no railway on Åland. Finland's VR network (https://www.vr.fi/en) is reached by sailing to Turku, and Sweden's SJ network via Stockholm - both are ferry journeys away. All travel on the islands is by road, bike or boat.

bus.note: No international coaches. Ålandstrafiken (https://www.alandstrafiken.ax/) runs the island bus network from Mariehamn out along the main roads, with services timed around the archipelago ferries. Cycling is genuinely the most popular way to get around, and bikes travel free or cheaply on the ferries.

intl.to: Helsinki & Tallinn (Estonia) - via the Åland stop

ferry.note: Mariehamn is a scheduled stop on the big Stockholm-Turku and Stockholm-Helsinki ferries, which is why the islands have such good connections for their size - the Åland call is what allows the tax-free shops on board. Crossings run year-round, several times a day in summer. Ålandstrafiken's smaller ferries link the outer archipelago islands, some of them free.

half.name: Kastelholm Castle
half.blurb: Medieval island castle in Sund, ~25 km northeast, with the Jan Karlsgården open-air museum nearby.

half.name: Bomarsund Fortress ruins
half.blurb: Atmospheric remains of a 19th-century Russian fortress destroyed in the Crimean War.

half.name: Eckerö Post and Customs House
half.blurb: Grand Engel-designed post house on Åland's western tip, once the empire's edge with Sweden.
